note: ZIP-215 redefines Ed25519 acceptance rules for cross-implementation compatibility. Key differences from RFC 8032: (1) non-canonical field element encodings are accepted as public keys or R-points; (2) all 8-torsion points (including identity) are accepted as public keys; (3) cofactored verification equation [8][s]B = [8]R + [8][k]A is used instead of [s]B = R + [k]A. This means signatures with s=0 over torsion-point public keys and R-points are valid under ZIP-215 for any message, because [8][0]B = O = [8]R + [8][k]A when both R and A have order dividing 8.

test_vectors.description: RFC 8032 Test 1 (empty message) — valid under both ZIP-215 and RFC 8032
Identity public key (order-1 torsion point) with zero scalar — ZIP-215 valid, strict-profile invalid, bare RFC 8032 VALID
test_vectors.note: Identity (order-1 torsion point) as public key, R = identity, s = 0. This vector is the one place the three profiles disagree, so it is worth stating precisely. Under a bare RFC 8032 verifier the check is [s]B = R + [k]A, i.e. O = O + [k]O = O, which HOLDS for any message: Go's crypto/ed25519 accepts it. RFC 8032 does not require rejecting small-order public keys anywhere — §5.1.3 fails only when x^2 has no square root or when x = 0 with the sign bit set (this encoding is canonical), and §5.1.7 offers the cofactored equation as an explicitly optional alternative, not an extra screen. The rejection recorded in valid_strict is therefore this repo's deliberate policy, shared with libsodium and ed25519-dalek's verify_strict, and not a spec mandate. An earlier revision of this file claimed 'RFC 8032 explicitly rejects identity as a valid public key'; that was wrong and is corrected here.

test_vectors.description: Order-2 torsion point public key with zero scalar — ZIP-215 valid, strict-profile invalid
test_vectors.note: Order-2 torsion point (the unique point of order 2 on the Ed25519 curve) as public key. R = same order-2 point, s = 0. ZIP-215 accepts via the cofactored equation. The strict profile rejects on its small-order screen. A bare RFC 8032 verifier also rejects, but for a different and weaker reason: the check becomes O = [1+k]P, which holds iff k is odd, so the answer depends on the message through k rather than on any rule about small-order keys. valid_rfc8032_cofactorless is false here because it is false for THIS message.

test_vectors.description: Order-8 torsion point public key (canonical encoding) with zero scalar — ZIP-215 valid, strict-profile invalid
test_vectors.note: Canonical encoding of an order-8 torsion point. This encoding is in libsodium's EXCLUDED_POINT_ENCODINGS list (rejected by legacy implementations). ZIP-215 explicitly accepts all torsion points including those previously excluded. As with tc_3, a bare RFC 8032 verifier rejects this for the message-dependent parity reason and not because of any small-order rule.

test_vectors.description: Non-canonical public key encoding of the identity — ZIP-215 valid, strict-profile invalid
test_vectors.note: Non-canonical encoding of the identity point. The canonical y-coordinate of the identity is 1 = 0x01. The value 2^255 - 18 = 0xedfff...ff7f is a non-canonical representation because the field prime p = 2^255 - 19, so edfff...ff7f = 1 (mod p). RFC 8032 §5.1.3 requires rejecting non-canonical encodings. ZIP-215 §2 explicitly accepts them. The signature R-point uses the same non-canonical encoding; s=0 makes it valid under ZIP-215's cofactored equation.

test_vectors.description: Both-invalid: scalar s not reduced mod ell — rejected by both ZIP-215 and RFC 8032
test_vectors.note: Signature with s > ell (scalar field order). ZIP-215 §3 requires s < ell; both ZIP-215 and RFC 8032 reject unreduced scalars.

verification_profiles.valid_zip215: ZIP-215 §2: cofactored equation [8][s]B = [8]R + [8][k]A, non-canonical encodings accepted, all 8-torsion points accepted as public keys.
verification_profiles.valid_strict: Historical, no target implements it any more: cofactorless RFC 8032 verification PLUS two screens RFC 8032 permits but does not mandate — canonical encodings only, and small-order (torsion) public keys rejected (libsodium / ed25519-dalek verify_strict). Until 2026-09-24 it was this repository's strict profile. The policy every target implements now is RFC 8032 as written (canonical decoding, S < L, cofactored equation, no small-order screen); its oracle is ed25519-policy-vectors.json, whose valid_rfc8032 column is that policy. On this file's six cases it accepts tc_1 to tc_4 and rejects tc_5 and tc_6.
verification_profiles.valid_rfc8032_cofactorless: A bare RFC 8032 §5.1.7 implementation with no added policy: decode, reject s >= L, check [s]B = R + [k]A. Go's crypto/ed25519 is exactly this, and these values were produced by running it over this corpus. It differs from valid_strict on tc_2 alone.
